data.name: Dunyana
data.gender_notes: Dunyana is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root duniyah, which means 'worldly' or 'of this world'. In Islamic context, it can refer to the material or temporal world, contrasting with the eternal and spiritual realm. The name Dunyana carries the meaning “Worldly” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Dunyana usually hope their child will grow to embody worldly and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the reminder to focus on the eternal and spiritual world while living in the material world.
data.etymology: Dunyana belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Worldly.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dunyana total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic philosophical and spiritual thought, placing too much emphasis or attachment on the "Dunyana", or material world, is often considered a departure from the path of righteousness and a hindrance to gaining spiritual enlightenment. This concept is emphasized in various Islamic texts and sayings of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the term "Dunyana" signifies the aspects of life that are temporary and fleeting, in contrast to the eternal and spiritual realm. Muslims are encouraged to strive for excellence and balance in both the material and spiritual worlds, with priority given to the latter. The ultimate goal in Islam is to seek the pleasure of Allah in both worlds and attain His nearness.
